original_card.question: Can one small, precisely scoped interface lemma be formalized with its actual hypotheses?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Read the exact hypotheses in the hyperplane-end proof and distinguish Lean theorems from finite supplier assumptions.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: State one missing boundary lemma in full before starting a proof-assistant build.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

actual_scope: Formalize weighted and uniform norm bounds for every prefix of the existing LemmaG.Stream event semantics under norm-preserving label maps, exact recipes and well-labelled execution; formalize the coordinate partial-store bound with explicit hypotheses.
scope_change_reason: Choose the formal-interface card, closing PR1282's explicit formalization handoff. Import the unchanged source definitions and theorem instead of rebuilding a parallel event model. The selected supplier's concrete all-prefix certificate and physical recipe binding remain separate.
bottleneck_link: A checked quantified prefix-norm implication reduces one precision-transfer proof gap while retaining concrete compiler/hosting assumptions. No new kappa or supplier admission.
stop_rule: One formal boundary package with explicit premise coverage, exact source/toolchain pins, axiom audit and nonvacuous examples. Do not extend into the full multiplication theorem or repeat the numeric certificate.
evidence: Lean 4.21.0 freshly compiled unchanged LemmaG.Stream and the new PrefixNorm/Examples modules in three workspaces, including a fresh dependency setup with the final runner. All 13 core and 20 example theorems passed the complete standard-axiom audit. A false undercharged partial-store theorem was rejected. Seven Python guard tests passed, including read-only isolated optimized relocation and source corruption. See VALIDATION.md; this is a quantified boundary proof, not formalization of the selected finite certificate.
author: Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with proof, code, validation and writing; no subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.blocked_by: A checked translation of events, extended labels, exact recipes, coefficient scratch and every relevant cut; the selected PR1094 word is not encoded here.

open_questions.blocked_by: Concrete native recipes, roundoff accumulation, hosting, physical compiler/tape accounting and all-size analytic transfer are outside this package.
